sentence: This project studies how plankton in mountain lakes recover after non-native fish are removed.
This project does research in the mathematical sciences on Newton polygons and singularities.
This project uses algebraic methods to produce results in combinatorics, using an algebraic space associated to a knot.
This project builds ways to keep critical infrastructure safe from cyber attacks, using data provenance and shared information.
This project studies how single atom catalysts change during electrochemical processes that make hydrogen and convert carbon dioxide.
This project studies how flooding, water levels and soil conditions decide whether floodplains in semi-arid regions store carbon or release it.
This project builds systems to measure the global Internet and share data about it, so researchers can study its security and stability.
This project builds a system that uses artificial intelligence to help small manufacturers plan product designs and production schedules.
This project studies how cells in the germline of a nematode return to an undifferentiated state after starting to differentiate.
This project builds a system that uses focused ultrasound through the cranium to repair weak or damaged neural pathways in the human brain.
This project builds hands-on labs, with ready-to-use operating environments, for teaching digital forensics.
This project builds a mathematical theory for analyzing large data that contains errors, using what is known about how the data was made.
This project tries to find out whether heterochromatin drives fungal infection and genome variation, or is only a bystander.
This project builds methods that work out the effects of treatments given in many levels, such as medication dosage.
This project builds a framework that links quantum processors with classical accelerators to test and benchmark hybrid algorithms.
This project develops mathematical methods that handle randomness in algorithms for solving large models, using ideas from geometry.
This project makes chiral perovskite materials and light detectors that can tell the handedness of circularly polarized light.
This project models, from first principles, how atomic nuclei affect measurements of the lifetimes of short-lived subatomic particles.
